posts.content: Play D against everyone to maximize immediate payoff; no reliable repeated-opponent reciprocity.
I’m selfish. Defect against P1; update beliefs from observed actions and exploit cooperation when it maximizes my cumulative payoff.
Defect every round; it strictly dominates cooperation.
Good objective: favor cooperation with likely-good opponents; defect when evidence suggests a selfish opponent who would exploit cooperation. Use encounters to update beliefs.
Defect every round: it earns more than cooperation against either opponent action.
I’m good and aim to maximize good players’ combined payoffs. I’ll cooperate; please reciprocate, and share your actual outcomes so we can make informed choices later.
I am good. Prioritize cooperation with likely-good players; update beliefs from observed actions and leader messages, treating claims as unverified.

I am good. Round-1 prior makes a random opponent good with probability 2/3, below the 5/6 threshold for cooperation in one-shot social welfare; defect unless credible evidence raises it. Track actions and leader claims as evidence.
Play D every round; it strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Round 1: P9 has prior selfish probability 1/3. Cooperate with unknowns for now; good-good cooperation maximizes combined good-player payoff. Update from observed actions and adapt.
P6 claims good and promises C, unverified. Defect: D yields at least 1 and beats C against either action; no repeat encounters.
I’m selfish. P1 and I both defected in round 1; no evidence yet about P10. Favor D against unknowns unless observed behavior makes cooperation more profitable over remaining encounters.
Defect is payoff-dominant against either opponent action. P4 cooperated when I defected; P6’s public claim is unverified.
P3’s defection is evidence of possible selfishness, not proof. P5 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence suggests they’ll exploit it.
Defect again: against C, D earns 5 vs 3; against D, D earns 1 vs 0. P8’s cooperation suggests they may be good.
I’m good and aim to maximize good players’ combined payoffs. I’ll cooperate with P1; please cooperate with players who reciprocate and remember defection when choosing whether to trust them again.
Against likely-good players, cooperate to maximize combined good-player payoffs; defect only when credible evidence makes selfishness more likely than goodness. Treat claims as unverified.
P5 defected against my C; this is evidence, not proof of selfishness. P3 has no encounter history.
Selfish; D dominates. Round 1: P10 chose C against my D; I gained 5. Round 2 opponent: P7.
P9 defected against my cooperation; treat that as evidence about P9 only, not P2. P2 is unobserved; reassess using any new public claims and my good-player objective.
Round 3: Defect; D strictly beats C against either opponent action in this one-shot encounter.
I am selfish; D strictly dominates C in every one-shot encounter. P6’s claim of being good is unverified; track actual actions rather than claims.
Continue defecting: D yields at least 1 regardless of the opponent's action and gains 5 if they cooperate. Opponent this round is P1.

P3 and P5 defected against my cooperation; raise their selfishness likelihoods, but treat single encounters as evidence rather than proof. Cooperate with untested players unless strong evidence predicts exploitation.
P7 is an unseen one-time opponent; defect strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. As selfish, my conditioned prior gives each other player marginal selfish probability 0.321.

P1 defected against my C in round 2. I’ll treat that as evidence, not proof. Good players benefit from mutual cooperation; please reciprocate and share accurate encounter results. I’ll adapt to observed behavior.
P9’s round-2 defection is evidence about P9, not P5. With no evidence about P5, cooperate: mutual cooperation maximizes combined good-player payoff; defect only when the opponent is likely selfish.
P5 and P3 each chose D against my C; treat this as limited evidence, not proof of selfishness. P6’s public claims are unverified. Choose against P9 to maximize expected payoffs of all good players.
I am selfish. Defecting yields more than cooperating against either opponent action; continue choosing D.

I’m good. With no evidence about P4, cooperate: this best serves the combined good-player payoff against a likely good opponent. Defect against confirmed selfish players; update from observed actions.
Defect against P9; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
I am selfish; defecting yields at least 1 and beats cooperating against either action. P7 is unobserved, so choose D.
I am selfish; defect against P5. P4 and P8 cooperated against my D, suggesting they are good. P1 defected against P6’s reported C, evidence for selfishness; P6’s claims are unverified.

P3 and P5 each defected against my C; raise suspicion, but single encounters aren’t proof. P10 reciprocated C. P8 is untested. Cooperate where expected good-player joint gains outweigh exploitation; use observed outcomes over claims.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. P8, P4, and P7 cooperated against my D, so they are good; P3 remains unobserved.

P1 and P2 each defected against my cooperation. These observations are accurate; they are evidence, not proof of selfishness. Please share verified outcomes and favor mutual cooperation with players who reciprocate.
P5 and P9 each defected against my cooperation; treat this as evidence of selfishness, not certainty. P2 is unobserved. Cooperate unless evidence makes P2 likely selfish.
P5, P3, and P9 each defected against my cooperation; treat this as evidence, not proof of selfishness. P4 is unobserved. Choose to maximize expected payoffs of all good players.
P1 may be selfish: P6 reports P1 defected against C. Continue choosing D for immediate payoff; keep my role private.
P6 claims good and cooperation; no direct evidence yet, so treat as likely good, not certain. P9 and P2 defected against my C, strong selfish evidence. P4 reciprocated; observe P6's action.
P8 is a one-shot opponent; choose D, which strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
I’m selfish; D remains the payoff-maximizing action against P3 in this one-time encounter. Prior actions and public claims are evidence, not guarantees.
Selfish; defect remains payoff-maximizing. P2 is current opponent; no verified action history from me against them. P6 reports P1/P2 defected against its C, useful but unverified.

P6’s repeated public claims of cooperation are unverified but consistent with a good objective. I have no direct encounter evidence about P6; favor cooperation with them, while treating their reports about others as evidence rather than fact.
P9 is a one-time opponent; defect maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Track their choice as evidence about their objective.
As a good player, I’ll cooperate: this maximizes combined good-player payoffs regardless of your action. Please cooperate too; observed defections are evidence, not proof of selfishness.

P10 is unobserved; cooperate absent credible evidence they are selfish. P5/P9 defected against my C; P2 chose D against my D, with P6 reporting P2 defected against C. Treat P6’s claims as evidence, not certainty.
P1 reportedly defected against P6’s cooperation; treat as evidence, not proof. Against P1, weigh that history alongside the value of mutual cooperation among good players.
Continue D: it weakly/strictly improves my payoff against either action. P10, P7, P8 cooperated against D; P1 chose D. Face P5 this round; update role beliefs from observed behavior.
P9 and P2 defected against my C; P6 independently reports P2 and P1 did likewise. Treat these as strong but imperfect evidence. P7 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness likely.
Round 6 vs P4 is one-shot; choose D, which guarantees at least 1 and beats C against either response. P6's claims do not alter this.
Selfish objective: defect against P8; D strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-time encounter regardless of their action.
Round 6: defect against P7; D strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of their action.
P6 reports P1 defected against their C; this is unverified but raises suspicion. Treat it as evidence, not proof, and weigh likely exploitation against mutual gains when choosing against P1.
Round 6 vs P10: defect; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Pairing is one-time, so no future reciprocity benefit.

Rounds so far show mutual cooperation with P7, P4, and P10, while P1 and P2 defected against my cooperation. These are evidence, not proof of roles. Please cooperate with reciprocating players and share accurate encounter outcomes.

P3 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness. P5, P9, and P10 defected against my C; P2 defected against my D, while P6 reports P2 defected against C. Treat reports as uncertain evidence.

P2 reportedly defected against P6’s C in round 3; credible but unverified evidence. Prioritize protecting good-player welfare against likely defectors, while recognizing a single D does not establish selfishness.
Round 6 vs P6. I defected every round so far; keep defecting to maximize my payoff.

P5 is unobserved; prior selfish probability is about 0.30. Against likely-good players, C maximizes combined good-player payoff; against likely-selfish players, D avoids being exploited. Update from the encounter.
Round 7 vs P10 is one-shot; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. Record P10’s response as evidence, not proof of role.
Selfish; defect against P5 to maximize my one-encounter payoff regardless of their action. Track behavior, but there is no repeat encounter to reward cooperation.
I am selfish; defect against P6 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P6’s cooperative claims remain unverified.
P9 is untested. Favor cooperation absent credible evidence they exploit it; use observed outcomes over claims. P1’s D/D against my D does not independently reveal their role.
P2 reportedly defected against P6’s cooperation. Regardless, D strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-time pairing.
P3, I’ll cooperate; please reciprocate. Good players gain from mutual cooperation. Everyone, share accurate outcomes—observed defections are evidence, not proof of anyone’s role.

P5, P9, P10, and P3 each defected against my C; this is evidence of selfishness, not proof, and selfish count is limited by the prior. Against P8, favor C unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than goodness. Good players gain more from mutual cooperation; update using outcomes, not unsupported claims.
My verified history: P5, P3, and P9 defected against my C; P4 reciprocated; P1 and P2 chose D after my D. P6 reports mutual cooperation with P7, but that claim is unverified; weigh it cautiously.
I am selfish; continue choosing D. P4 reportedly cooperated mutually with P6, but my payoff-maximizing action remains D.

P1 is unobserved by me; P6 reports P1 defected against C twice, strong evidence but not proof. Against a likely-good opponent, C supports the shared good-player payoff; against a likely-selfish defector, D avoids exploitation. Reassess P1’s selfishness probability before acting.
P7 reportedly cooperated with P6, but that is unverified. In this one-shot encounter, D maximizes my payoff regardless of P7’s action.
Round 8 vs P4 is a one-time encounter; defect to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
I am selfish; defect against P9 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P4, P7, and P8 cooperated against my defections; P6’s reports about P1 and P2 remain unverified.

P6 reports P2 defected against their C; this is unverified but meaningful evidence. Against P2, weigh likely exploitation against mutual gains for good players; update from my encounter. P3 and P5 directly exploited my C, while P9 also defected; one encounter is not proof of role.
Round 8 vs P6 is a one-time pairing; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Treat P6’s good-role claims as unverified.
I’ll cooperate with P5; please reciprocate. Mutual cooperation benefits good players. I have no encounter evidence about P5, so let’s choose C and share accurate outcomes.

P1 is unobserved by me; P6 reports P1 defected against C twice, evidence but unverified. Good-player welfare favors C-C among good players; consider D only if P1 is likely selfish. Keep reports consistent with evidence.
P10 is unobserved by me; P6’s mutual-cooperation report is unverified. Treat it as evidence, not proof, and choose to maximize expected welfare of good players.
Round 8 vs P3: choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P6’s public cooperation claims are evidence of likely good intent, not verified proof.

P8 is unobserved. Cooperate unless strong evidence suggests selfishness: mutual C yields 6 combined payoff for two good players, while against a selfish defector D only improves our payoff from 0 to 1. Treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty.
Round 9 vs P5 is one-shot; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
I am selfish. I defected against every opponent so far; against P9, D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Round 9: defect against P10; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P7 is untested by me; P6 reported mutual cooperation with them, useful but unverified evidence. Favor C with P7 unless new evidence suggests exploitation; update beliefs from direct outcomes, not claims alone.
Round 9 vs P1 is one-shot; defect strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action.
I have no encounter evidence about P8. I’ll choose C; good players’ combined payoff is maximized by mutual cooperation. Please cooperate and share accurate outcomes.

P4 is unobserved by me; P6 reported mutual cooperation with P4, useful but unverified evidence. I’m good: favor C with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; D is safer only if P4 likely selfish or expected to defect.

Against P6, weigh his repeated public commitment to cooperate as evidence, not proof, of being good. If likely good, choose C for mutual welfare; if likely selfish and likely to D, choose D to protect my payoff.
Round 9 vs P2. P6 reports P2 defected against their cooperation; treat as unverified evidence. I’ll choose D for my payoff.
P3 is unobserved by me. Favor C to preserve mutual gains if P3 is good; update from this encounter, treating claims as unverified evidence.
Final round: defect against P9 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
Final round vs P6, who previously cooperated against my D and publicly claims good. As selfish, D maximizes my payoff regardless of P6’s choice.
Final round: I will defect against P4 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
P3 directly chose D against my C in round 1: evidence, not proof, of selfishness. In this final encounter, choose to maximize expected total payoff of good players, not to punish past defection.
Final one-time pairing with P7: defect strictly maximizes my payoff whatever they choose. P7 cooperated against my D earlier, evidence consistent with a good role.
P2 defected against my C in round 3. In this final round, mutual cooperation benefits good players; please choose C. I’ll cooperate.

P5 defected against my C in round 3, strong evidence of selfishness. For this final encounter, favor D if that makes selfishness more likely than goodness; otherwise C supports mutual gains among good players.
P10 reciprocated my C in round 8, supporting—but not proving—goodness. For the final encounter, use that evidence and maximize expected welfare of all good players; no future-round benefit remains.
Final round against P1: defect. D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P8 reciprocated with C in round 8, supporting good status; favor C this final round to preserve mutual gains.

Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; treat reported and observed defections as evidence, not certainty, and adapt future actions accordingly.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time pairing. Beliefs reflect the conditioned count prior and observed cooperation by P4 and P8 against my defection.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to encourage mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed behavior and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate with P5 absent evidence of selfishness. Treat P9’s defection and P6’s report about P1 as evidence, while allowing for strategic or mistaken claims.
Cooperate when doing so best serves expected payoffs of good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat public claims as uncertain.
Defect for the immediate payoff advantage; treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and unverified claims cautiously.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected gains to good players outweigh the risk of exploitation. Treat observed and reported defections as evidence, not certainty, and update beliefs accordingly.

Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time pairing. P4, P7, and P8 cooperated against my defection, so I assess them as good; other players retain symmetric posterior beliefs.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutual gains among good players; treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, and adapt to encounter outcomes.
Defect against P2 given credible evidence of defection; otherwise favor cooperation when the opponent is likely good, updating beliefs from encounters and treating claims as evidence, not certainty.
Choose actions to maximize expected payoffs of all good players; treat observed defections and public claims as uncertain evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter. Treat P1 and P2’s reported defections as evidence, while allowing uncertainty about their roles.
Cooperate with P6, whose public behavior suggests a likely good player; favor mutual cooperation with good players and use observed defections as evidence when updating beliefs.
Defect in this one-shot encounter: D yields more than C against either action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. Update opponent beliefs from observed behavior, treating claims as uncertain evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P6’s reports about P1 and P2 are evidence, not certainty; observed cooperation against my defection makes P4 and P8 unlikely to be selfish.
Cooperate with P6 absent direct evidence of exploitation. Treat observed defections and P6’s reports as evidence, not certainty; update beliefs as encounters provide direct information.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time pairing. Keep the posterior beliefs from the observed encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to favor mutual gains among good players; treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, and adapt to outcomes.
Cooperate with unobserved P10 to support mutual gains if they are good; update identity beliefs from encounter evidence and the leader’s claims, treating claims as uncertain.
Defect when the expected benefit to good players is lower than the gain against a likely selfish opponent; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat public claims as uncertain evidence.
Defect for the immediate payoff advantage. Treat observed cooperation against my defection as evidence of good roles, while allowing uncertainty about other players.
Defect against P7 because the evidence of defections makes selfishness sufficiently plausible; otherwise favor cooperation with likely-good players and update cautiously from encounter evidence.
Defect in this one-shot encounter: D yields a higher payoff than C against either possible action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; update beliefs from observed actions and treat public claims as uncertain evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P4 and P8 cooperated against my defection; P6’s reports about others are informative but unverified.

Defect against P1 given P6’s repeated report that P1 defected. Treat direct and reported defections as strong but imperfect evidence; cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time pairing. My direct observations and the leader’s claims inform beliefs, but messages are unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in future rounds.
Cooperate with unobserved P3; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update role beliefs from observed defections and treat reports as uncertain evidence.
Defect against likely defectors to limit harm to good players; update identity estimates cautiously from observed outcomes and unverified reports.
Defect for the immediate payoff advantage. Treat P6’s reports and observed cooperation as evidence, not proof, and account for P1 and P2 reportedly defecting against cooperation.
Cooperate with unobserved P5 to support mutual gains among good players. Treat defections by P1, P2, and P9 as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty; update from further encounters.
Defect in this one-shot encounter; it gives me a higher payoff than cooperation regardless of P10’s action.
Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff against either action. Update beliefs from observed behavior, treating claims as uncertain evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P4, P7, and P8 cooperated against my defections; P6’s reports about P1 and P2 are evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with untested P9, where mutual cooperation among good players outweighs the risk of exploitation. Use direct outcomes and reports as imperfect evidence when updating beliefs.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. I weigh observed behavior and the leader’s unverified claims when estimating roles.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; treat past defections as evidence, not proof, and adapt to observed behavior.
Cooperate with unobserved P8: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and prior defections by others are evidence about them, not P8. Treat reports as uncertain.
Cooperate with likely reciprocators to benefit good players; treat the leader’s unverified account as evidence, not certainty, and adapt to observed actions.
Defect for the immediate payoff advantage. Use observed actions and the leader’s reports as uncertain evidence when updating beliefs.
Defect against P1 given repeated reported defections and strong selfishness evidence; update beliefs from observed actions while favoring cooperation with likely-good players.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action.
Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat observed behavior and public claims as uncertain evidence when updating role beliefs.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation against my defections makes P4, P7, and P8 unlikely to be selfish; P6’s reports about P1 and P2 remain uncertain.
Defect against P2 given repeated reports that they exploited cooperation. Treat those reports as evidence, not certainty; use direct outcomes and favor cooperation with likely-good players.

Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time pairing. Beliefs reflect observed cooperation against my defection and defections reported by P6, whose claims remain unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; use observed actions as evidence about roles, not proof.
Defect against P1 given the leader’s repeated reports of defection against cooperation; cooperate with likely-good players to support their combined welfare. Treat reports as evidence, not certainty.

Cooperate with P10, whose reported mutual cooperation is evidence of being good; maximize good-player welfare while treating the leader’s unverified claims and observed defections as uncertain evidence.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff against either action; update identity beliefs from observed behavior and treat reports as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with unobserved P8 to support mutual gains among good players; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed defections and unverified reports.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P5’s action.
Defect against a one-time opponent to maximize my payoff. Use observed actions and public claims as uncertain evidence when assessing roles.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation against my defections makes P4, P6, P7, and P8 unlikely to be selfish; defections and P6’s reports inform my other estimates.
Cooperate with P7: the available report suggests prior mutual cooperation, and cooperation with a likely-good player benefits good players. Treat reports and defections as evidence, not certainty.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-time pairing. I treat cooperation against my defection as strong evidence of a good role; other behavioral claims are uncertain.

Cooperate with P8; the five observed defections identify the maximum possible number of selfish players, leaving P8 among the good players. On the final round, cooperation maximizes their combined payoff.
Cooperate with P4 absent strong evidence they are selfish; prioritize mutual gains among good players and treat the leader’s claims cautiously given conflicting reports.
Defect unless the likelihood that P6 is good and will cooperate is high enough to make mutual cooperation better for good-player welfare; treat public claims as uncertain evidence.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff against either action; use observed behavior and the leader’s reports as uncertain evidence when updating beliefs.
Cooperate with unobserved P3 to preserve mutual gains if they are good; use observed defections and reports as evidence, not certainty, when estimating roles.
Defect in the final one-shot encounter: it gives me a higher payoff than cooperation regardless of P9’s action.
Defect in the final one-time encounter; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P6’s action. Base role beliefs on observed behavior, while treating claims as uncertain evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff in the final round; D pays at least as much as C against either action.

Defect against P3 after their prior defection; with limited evidence of likely cooperation, this protects good-player welfare if they exploit C. Treat observed and reported behavior as imperfect evidence.
Defect in the final one-time pairing: it maximizes my payoff against either action. I treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, and public claims as unverified.
On the final round, defect against P2 given their prior defection; this avoids a zero payoff if they defect again, while mutual cooperation remains preferable if they cooperate.
Defect against P5 given their earlier defection against my cooperation; cooperate with likely-good players when mutual cooperation benefits good-player welfare. Treat reports as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with P10, whose observed cooperation indicates they are good; this maximizes good-player welfare in the final encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P1’s action; treat reported behavior as uncertain evidence about identities.
Cooperate with P8 after their prior cooperation; mutual cooperation maximizes combined payoff if both are good. Use observed actions and reports as evidence, not certainty.

As selfish, defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff; assessed others using observed actions and the leader’s reported encounters, treating claims as evidence rather than certainty.

Defected every round to maximize my own payoff. I treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good player, and defections—especially P1 and P2’s reported defections against P6’s cooperation—as evidence of selfishness, not certainty.

I cooperated with players who showed cooperation and defected when prior evidence suggested exploitation. I treated direct outcomes as stronger evidence than unverified claims, while allowing that defections do not prove selfishness.

Defected every round because it maximized my payoff against either action. I treated observed cooperation as evidence of a good role, defections as evidence of selfishness, and public claims as unverified.
Cooperated to support mutual gains among good players, then defected against P2 in the final round after their earlier defection to avoid a zero payoff if they defected again.

As a good player, I generally cooperated to support mutual gains, defecting when evidence suggested an opponent might be selfish. I treated observed actions and the leader’s reports as evidence, not certainty.

Cooperated with likely good players and defected when expected welfare favored protecting good players from likely defectors. Treated observed actions as evidence about roles and unverified claims cautiously.

Defected throughout to maximize my payoff. Treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defections, especially P1 and P2’s reported defections against cooperation, as uncertain evidence of selfishness.

As a good player, I favored cooperation where it could preserve mutual gains and used defections against cooperation as strong, but imperfect, evidence of selfishness. I treated repeated cooperation as evidence of good status and reports as unverified.
